title: Stage 4 Breakdown, Multi-Timeframe Structure and Stop-Loss Breach

epigraph.quote: The trend is your friend until the bend at the end.
epigraph.author: Market maxim

web_blocks.text: TARIL's chart has broken down since our 12 November 2026 dossier. On 25 November 2026, live TradingView closed at ₹287.95 (-0.52% 1D, -5.90% 1W, -3.70% 1M, -5.28% 3M, -10.57% 6M). That followed a verified 23 November 2026 NSE ledger close of ₹289.45 (-2.57% 1D, -6.25% 1W, -7.97% 1M). Both closes decisively breached our prior ₹292.47 structural stop-loss: -1.03% below stop on the 23 November ledger and -1.55% below stop on 25 November live TradingView. The live TradingView engine now classifies TARIL as STAGE_4 with posture AVOID_STAGE4_OR_BROKEN and timing gate CAP_REJECTED. [41]

Comparing both feeds shows the exact shift into breakdown. The 23 November NSE ledger still prints Stage 1 (Basing) at ₹289.45, yet price already sat below the 20D SMA (₹308.01), 50D SMA (₹299.08), 200D SMA (₹302.94), and approx 10W EMA (₹304.27). Daily RSI was 39.69, with 5 distribution days in 25 sessions, -15.17% 28-day RS, and -3.10% 63-day RS. By 25 November, live TradingView confirms full Stage 4 failure at ₹287.95. Price now sits 4.10% below the 10W EMA (₹300.26), 3.81% below the 50D SMA (₹299.36), 5.16% below the 200D SMA (₹303.62), and 6.62% below the 30W SMA (₹308.35). Every major average from the 10D SMA (₹304.57) to the 40W EMA (₹312.95) now acts as overhead resistance. [41]

Weekly, daily, and four-hour frames all confirm bearish momentum with no reversal. On the 25 November weekly chart, RSI slipped to 44.61 and price sits 22.59% below its ₹372.00 52-week high (versus -22.19% on the 23 November ledger; both feeds match the ₹224.05–₹372.00 range). Daily RSI is 38.61 (39.69 on ledger), with a -0.42 overall TradingView rating and -0.93 moving-average rating. On the four-hour frame, RSI fell to 31.70 beneath the 4H EMA20 (₹300.96) and 4H SMA50 (₹308.56). The options package flags STAGE4_BELOW_STRUCTURAL_FLOOR with intraday_4h_turn = false. No bottoming turn is present. [41]

Volume confirms buyers are absent. On 25 November, TARIL traded 944,033 shares—just 0.20x its 30-day average of 4,759,244 shares (versus 1,184,343 shares, or 0.67x 20D average, on 23 November). Bollinger bandwidth is 11.94% and ATR14 is ₹10.98 on TradingView (₹11.53 on ledger). Both our prior ₹299.92–₹314.51 support zone and the ₹292.47 hard stop failed without attracting institutional bids. The next chart shelf sits down at Pivot S1 ₹259.33 (reference band ₹255.44–₹263.22; chart invalidation ₹253.84), followed by Pivot S2 at ₹220.37 near the ₹224.05 52-week low. [41]

web_blocks.takeaway: Both the 23 November NSE ledger and 25 November live TradingView closes sit below the ₹292.47 prior structural stop, with price beneath all major daily, weekly, and four-hour moving averages. [41]

web_blocks.text: Broad market context makes TARIL's break even clearer. On 23 November, the Nifty 50 regime was 'Uptrend (narrow breadth)': 55.2% of stocks stood above their 50D SMA, 48.2% above their 200D SMA, 7 of 11 sectors above key averages, and just 3 distribution days in 25 sessions. TARIL lagged this uptrend by -15.17% over 28 sessions while printing 5 distribution days. Domestic transformer peers broke down too: CG Power (-10.75% vs 30W SMA) and Voltamp (-4.01% vs 30W SMA) sit in Stage 4, while Hitachi Energy India sits in Stage 1 (-7.73% vs 30W SMA). Capital is leaving transformer OEMs for cleaner Stage 2 leaders. [41]

Our upward-only stop-loss ratchet is strictly binding. The 12 November dossier set TARIL's hard stop at ₹292.47. We never lower a stop-loss to chase a falling stock down to a lower pivot shelf (₹255.44–₹263.22 / ₹253.84). Because TARIL closed below ₹292.47 on both 23 November (₹289.45) and 25 November (₹287.95), the exit rule has triggered. The mandatory action for all 150 Zerodha shares is EXIT_IMMEDIATELY. Keeping ₹292.47 as the official stop caps a small -6.5% to -6.9% loss on a 1.02% weight before it turns into a 20%–45% Stage 4 drawdown. New capital gets zero allocation (TIER_0, REJECTED). Treat ₹255.44–₹263.22 strictly as a passive chart shelf, not a buy zone. [41]

The tape aligns with our Pass 1 forensics. Stocks rarely break their 50-day, 200-day, and 30-week averages on five distribution days while the Nifty 50 rises. Here, price mirrors the shareholder register: DIIs dropped from 7.68% to 1.19%, FIIs cut from 11.33% to 6.98%, debt jumped 27% in six months to ₹581 crore, and two external CEOs resigned amid World Bank Case No. 788. When a broken stop confirms institutional exit and rising debt, obeying the stop is the right call. [42][43][46]

Listed options offer no hedge here. The 25 November options snapshot marks TARIL NOT_OPTIONABLE_OR_ILLIQUID because it is not in the NSE F&O segment. There is no liquid options chain, no open options position, and no options trade. Risk must be managed strictly in cash equity—making the ₹292.47 exit trigger non-negotiable. [41]

web_blocks.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
paragraphs: Stops exist so that you never have to negotiate with a Stage 4 breakdown. TARIL broke ₹292.47 while Nifty 50 remained in an uptrend and DIIs exited the register. Moving the stop lower to ₹253 would turn a disciplined 1% portfolio risk check into an open-ended hope trade.

book_paragraphs: In our previous twelve November dossier, TARIL sat on a narrow technical ledge at three hundred fifteen rupees eighty paise, clinging just above its thirty-week average with a clear structural stop-loss drawn at two hundred ninety-two rupees forty-seven paise. Two weeks later, the ledge has given way. On twenty-three November two thousand twenty-six, the verified NSE market-facts ledger recorded a close of two hundred eighty-nine rupees forty-five paise, down two point five seven percent on the day and six point two five percent over one week. Two sessions later, on twenty-five November, the live TradingView snapshot showed a further slip to two hundred eighty-seven rupees ninety-five paise. Both closes sit cleanly below our two hundred ninety-two rupees forty-seven paise hard stop. When the market answers your risk line with a decisive break, the time for debate is over.

Let us walk through every timeframe carefully so you can see why this is a textbook Stage Four breakdown rather than a harmless one-day shakeout. On the weekly chart—the primary compass of Stan Weinstein's stage analysis—TARIL now trades six point six two percent below its thirty-week simple moving average of three hundred eight rupees thirty-five paise and four point one zero percent below its ten-week exponential moving average of three hundred rupees twenty-six paise. Weekly RSI has faded to forty-four point six one, and the stock has lost ten point five seven percent over six months while sitting twenty-two point five nine percent below its three hundred seventy-two rupee fifty-two-week high. Every rally attempt toward three hundred ten rupees now runs straight into trapped overhead supply from investors who bought the autumn consolidation.

Drop down to the daily chart and the damage is just as uniform. On the twenty-five November live TradingView tape, TARIL sits below its ten-day simple moving average at three hundred four rupees fifty-seven paise, its twenty-day average at three hundred seven rupees thirty-four paise, its fifty-day average at two hundred ninety-nine rupees thirty-six paise, and its two-hundred-day average at three hundred three rupees sixty-two paise. The verified twenty-three November NSE ledger confirms the exact same overhead ceiling, placing the twenty-day, fifty-day, and two-hundred-day averages at three hundred eight, two hundred ninety-nine, and three hundred three rupees, respectively. Daily RSI has dropped to thirty-eight point six one on TradingView and thirty-nine point six nine on the NSE ledger. TradingView's composite moving-average rating reads minus zero point nine three—nearly a unanimous sell across short-, medium-, and long-term moving averages.

What about the four-hour tactical frame, where early bottoming reversals usually appear first? There is no sign of a turn. On the twenty-five November four-hour snapshot, RSI has fallen to thirty-one point seven zero, price trades far below both the four-hour twenty-period exponential average at three hundred rupees ninety-six paise and the fifty-period simple average at three hundred eight rupees fifty-six paise, and the deterministic chart engine explicitly flags the setup as Stage Four Below Structural Floor with no intraday four-hour turn present. Oversold four-hour readings inside a Stage Four decline are not buy signals; they are symptoms of sustained selling pressure that frequently lead to brief dead-cat bounces into overhead resistance before making lower lows.

Notice also the small labeling difference between our two market data feeds, and why the live Stage Four classification governs. The verified twenty-three November NSE ledger still prints Stage One Basing at two hundred eighty-nine rupees forty-five paise because its slower trailing fifty-day slope had not yet rolled over completely, even though it already logged five distribution days in twenty-five sessions and a steep minus fifteen point one seven percent twenty-eight-day relative strength reading. By twenty-five November, the live TradingView stage engine downgraded TARIL unambiguously to Stage Four with an entry posture of Avoid Stage Four or Broken and a technical timing ceiling of Cap Rejected. Either way you slice the data, price has broken the two hundred ninety-two rupees forty-seven paise structural stop and sits beneath every single moving average that matters.

Compare TARIL's tape with the broader Indian market and you see why this weakness is company- and subsector-specific rather than a macro accident. On twenty-three November, the Nifty fifty regime remained in an Uptrend with narrow breadth: fifty-five point two percent of the top five hundred stocks stood above their fifty-day averages, seven of eleven sectors traded above their twenty-, fifty-, and two-hundred-day lines, and the benchmark carried just three distribution days in twenty-five sessions. Against that constructive backdrop, TARIL lagged the market by more than fifteen percent over twenty-eight sessions while absorbing five distribution days. Yet TARIL is not alone inside the domestic transformer cohort: CG Power sits ten point seven five percent below its thirty-week average in Stage Four, Voltamp sits four percent below its thirty-week average in Stage Four, and even mighty Hitachi Energy India has pulled back to Stage One twenty-three percent off its high. Institutional money is actively rotating out of power-transformer equipment makers.

Volume confirms that no deep-pocketed buyer is stepping in to catch the falling knife. On twenty-five November, TARIL traded roughly nine hundred forty-four thousand shares—just zero point two zero times its thirty-day average volume of four point seven six million shares. On twenty-three November, turnover was one point one eight million shares, or zero point six seven times its twenty-day average. Thin volume during a breakdown below key support means institutional demand has vanished. That technical observation dovetails cleanly with our Pass One forensic discovery: domestic institutional investors slashed their ownership from seven point six eight percent in December two thousand twenty-four to one point one nine percent in September two thousand twenty-six, while retail shareholder count more than doubled past two hundred twenty-three thousand. Retail holders rarely organize the sustained institutional accumulation required to lift a stock back above a broken thirty-week average.

This brings us to the single most important risk-management rule in our entire playbook: the upward-only stop-loss ratchet. When you already own shares—here, one hundred fifty shares held in Zerodha at an average cost of three hundred nine rupees forty-two paise—you are strictly forbidden from lowering a prior structural stop-loss to accommodate a falling share price. The TradingView pivot engine calculates the next lower horizontal support shelf at Pivot S1 around two hundred fifty-nine rupees thirty-three paise, with a reference band of two hundred fifty-five rupees forty-four paise to two hundred sixty-three rupees twenty-two paise and a chart invalidation at two hundred fifty-three rupees eighty-four paise. An undisciplined investor looks at that lower shelf and says, 'Let me move my stop down from two hundred ninety-two to two hundred fifty-three and give the stock more room.' That single habit destroys portfolios.

We refuse to move the stop down. Our structural stop remains locked at two hundred ninety-two rupees forty-seven paise. Because both the twenty-three November ledger close of two hundred eighty-nine rupees forty-five paise and the twenty-five November live close of two hundred eighty-seven rupees ninety-five paise breached that level, the exit rule has fired. Exiting all one hundred fifty shares immediately crystallizes a modest unrealized loss of roughly three thousand to three thousand two hundred twenty rupees—about six point five to six point nine percent on a one percent portfolio position—and frees roughly forty-three thousand two hundred to forty-three thousand four hundred rupees of capital before the stock tests two hundred fifty-nine rupees or worse.

Finally, do not look to the options market for a clever hedge or collar. Our twenty-five November options snapshot confirms that TARIL is not in the NSE futures and options segment and is classified as not optionable or illiquid. There is no listed put option to buy for downside protection, no covered call to sell against the shares, and no LEAPS structure to cap risk. Cash equity is the only arena available, which makes obeying the cash-equity stop-loss your only real line of defense.

What would it take for TARIL's chart to earn a second look in the future? Write down three concrete, non-negotiable technical milestones. First, the stock must stop making lower lows and build a multi-month Stage One base—whether near the two hundred fifty-five to two hundred sixty-three rupee Pivot S1 shelf or lower near the two hundred twenty-four rupee fifty-two-week low. Second, price must reclaim a flattening or rising thirty-week moving average on expanding institutional volume well above its thirty-day average, accompanied by rising relative strength against the Nifty fifty. Third, that technical repair must coincide with fundamental proof that working capital is falling below one hundred twenty days, operating cash flow has turned decisively positive, and the World Bank sanctions proceeding has been cleanly resolved. Until all three appear together, the tape is flashing red.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
book_callouts.text: The hardest loss to take is a small six-percent loss on a company whose order book still sounds exciting. Yet taking that small loss when the two hundred ninety-two rupee stop breaks is precisely what keeps you out of a forty-percent Stage Four trap.
